page: Microsoft Azure D8s_v3 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DSv3 server family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 processor running at 2.3 GHz. The instance features 8 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The processor includes a 50 MB L3 cache, 32 KB L1d cache, and 0.25 MB L2 cache, with support for AVX, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA instruction sets.

This virtual machine runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It includes 66 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, allowing users to attach high-performance persistent disks. There are no bundled GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses included with this instance type.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the D8s_v3 is positioned in the lower-to-average performance tiers. Single-core CPU performance is weak, as evidenced by a stress-ng single-core score of 1246.28 and a Geekbench single-core score of 848.0. Multi-core performance is relatively stronger, reaching an average tier with a stress-ng multi-core score of 6563.83, though Geekbench multi-core remains weak at 3121.0. Memory bandwidth is generally constrained, with uncached large-block read and write speeds of 35.34 GB/sec and 21.67 GB/sec respectively. However, the instance demonstrates average capabilities in small-model LLM inference, processing 411.44 tokens per second for prompts and generating 157.1 tokens per second using a 135M parameter model.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D8s_v3 offers a balanced resource density suitable for legacy enterprise workloads that require dedicated CPU allocation and moderate memory capacity without demanding high-frequency single-core execution. Given its performance profile, the instance is best suited for general-purpose workloads, moderate web serving, basic database operations, and lightweight multi-threaded applications that do not require intensive cryptographic or decompression throughput.
